Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Health | National Bawumia calls for amendment of Act 525 to strengthen CHAG’s role in healthcare delivery Source : Prince Adu-Owusu 16 November 2026 3:49pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has called for an amendment of Act 525 to formally integrate the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG) into the country's healthcare delivery system.
He said the current arrangement, which relies on Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs), should be replaced with a more institutionalised partnership that recognises CHAG's contribution to healthcare delivery.
Dr Bawumia made the proposal after meeting the leadership of CHAG as part of his engagements with various stakeholders across the country.
He noted that although the association accounts for about 6 per cent of Ghana's health infrastructure, its 42 health facilities deliver between 30 per cent and 40 per cent of the country's health services.
"What is clear is that CHAG is doing an amazing job under difficult circumstances," he said.
He explained that the association plays a significant role in providing healthcare in rural districts, particularly to poor and vulnerable communities.
"In the area of health, we agreed that Act 525 should be amended to mainstream CHAG rather than working through MOUs," Dr Bawumia stated.
The former Vice President also highlighted the need for additional incentives for health personnel working in rural communities to encourage them to serve in underserved areas.
He said discussions with the CHAG leadership also covered the removal of import duties on medical equipment to facilitate the retooling of health facilities.
On education, Dr Bawumia reiterated his commitment, as outlined in the New Patriotic Party's 2024 manifesto, to strengthen government partnerships with faith-based organisations.
He specifically reaffirmed his position on partnering with religious organisations to take over the management of mission schools.
He said the engagements were aimed at developing concrete policy proposals to address the challenges confronting CHAG and improve healthcare delivery across the country.
"I thank the leadership of CHAG for their participation in the meetings, and my team will continue our engagement and come out with concrete policies to address the challenges facing CHAG in particular and healthcare delivery in general," he added.
